issue_context.title: Output is modified when module set no_log to True.
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY

When Ansible 2.10.0a1 under Azure there might happen that the output of a
task is changed if a module uses no_log = True for an attribute.

For example, if the output of the module should contain "changed: True", and
an attribute with no_log set contains the value `hang` it might happen that
the output is modified to "c******ed: True", and if this output is further
processed (registering the result and comparing the value of `changed`),
the test might fail, but not because of module code, but because of unexpected
output processing.

This behavior was, currently, only reproduced with Ansible 2.10.0a1 running
under Azure. I did not have 2.10.0b1 to test it.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME

ansible output

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
2.10.0a1

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
Controler: Ubuntu 18.04, on Azure
Targets: Centos 8.1, also on Azure

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE

With a module that has a variable with "no_log" set to True, set the value of variable to `hang`, the output contains `c******ed: True`.

It was easy to reproduce with [ansible-freeipa](https://github.com/freeipa/ansible-freeipa) module ipavault.

##### EXPECTED RESULTS

If the value in the output is not part of the attribute, it should not be hidden.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS

Several string matching the attribute value in the output are modified to `******`.

This is expected.  We were made aware of a shortcoming in our `no_log` heuristics that could allow the `no_log` values to show up in keys, whereas previously we only restricted to values.  This was done in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/69653 but was not backported for reasons of a backwards incompatible change made in a minor release.

If you have further questions please stop by IRC or the mailing list:

   * IRC: #ansible on irc.freenode.net
   * mailing list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/ansible-project

The problem with this expected behavior is that if you have one single character in the field set to no log, you get an output like this:
```
ok: [cos81.ipa.test] => {
    "********hanged": true,
    "changed": false,
    "invo********ation": {
        "module_args": {
            "a********tion": "vault",
            "data": "VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER",
            "datafile_in": null,
            "datafile_out": null,
            "des********ription": null,
            "groups": null,
            "ipaadmin_password": "VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER",
            "ipaadmin_prin********ipal": "admin",
            "name": [
                "asymvault"
            ],
            "new_password": null,
            "new_password_file": null,
            "ownergroups": null,
            "owners": null,
            "ownerservi********es": null,
            "servi********e": null,
            "servi********es": null,
            "shared": null,
            "state": "present",
            "username": null,
            "users": null,
            "vault_data": "VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER",
            "vault_password": null,
            "vault_password_file": null,
            "vault_private_key": null,
            "vault_private_key_file": null,
            "vault_publi********_key": null,
            "vault_publi********_key_file": null,
            "vault_salt": null,
            "vault_type": null
        }
    }
}
```
Note that this output is actually **wrong**, as it says `ok`, but the correct result should be `changed`, as there were changes and they were reported by the module. The value of the field with `no_log` was set to `c`. Note that there are two entries for "changed" (`changed` and `********hanged`), with different values. The correct one here is the one that had the key name masked.
I do not understand why the no_log key name is replaced in all other keys as a sub string. I can understand that a key with the same name might be replaced though.

With the current behavior, I can even hide a failed module execution:

```yaml
  - name: Archive data value `data` to asymmetric vault
    ipavault:
      name: asymvault
      data: failed
      state: retrieved
``` 

The `data` attribute has `no_log` set, and this task should fail, but when I execute this, the result is "ok". If I change the value of data to be "foobar" it fails as expected.

If my module has a field ABC that is returned to the user, and the user password is "ABC", my module will not work because my key will be stripped.

Why strip key at all? What does it bring to improve security?
The password is not in the log, but having a look at the missing parts of the parameters reveals it. The parameter name or name part that is missing is the password.

Thank you.

The changes in #70762 seem to fix the problem.

review_comments: We aren't likely to have some of these, like `rc`, `stdout`, but it's not harmful I don't think, and isn't a required change.  In fact it's probably nice, as it gives others a good list to look at.
Right, it's not harmful, and is instructive.
Would we only want these keys to be skipped at the toplevel?

I don't think so. A user may want to specify keys that might appear at any depth, and maybe even multiple times. And it wouldn't make sense to hide a no_log value in a key at the top level, but not at a lower level, since that defeats the purpose.
Err, I meant "hide at a lower level but not at the top level", but I hope you see what I meant.

This should be moved up into the previous condition.  You can add both of these to the tuple that contains NoneType.

(I've commented on a bug where this should be changed in the `_remove_values_conditions()` function as well: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/70639 )
By "moved up", I mean, "merged into", in case that was not clear.

fwiw, the `chain` here isn't necessary. Python will traverse sub tuples. 

```pycon
>>> isinstance(True, (str, (bool,)))
True
```

This seems like the heart of something unmentioned in the changelogs but it doesn't seem okay to do... at least, not without a deprecation period.  Changing keys by default isn't without its drawbacks but anyone who depends upon it to keep secure values hidden will run into problems with this.

I think I heard something about the problem being with specific keys which should not be removed (like `changed` or `failed` ?).  If so, those could go into an always_allow list of some sort.  Another alternative which is something of a compromise might be to allow toplevel keys to be output unchanged but to continue to remove values on any keys inside of toplevel containers.

This change was new to 2.10, and after discussing it with prodsec, and the core eng team, we decided to revert this general change, and push the change onto module authors, thus handling it in `uri` specifically at this time.

@abadger This comes from a change that was merged for 2.10 so it's not yet released. We are basically reverting most of 69653 (I'm keeping the test that was added though) and replacing with this code that is specific for the uri module. You are right and folks are complaining that we should not modify the keys with such a big hammer (see issue #70455).
<nod> yeah.  I thought I had added it back in early 2.x but my memory was faulty.  Objection here withdrawn :-)
